summary.text: Rick Hillenbrand is a Republican member of the West Virginia House of Delegates, representing District 88 in Hampshire and Mineral counties, and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A retired U.S. Navy commander and engineer, he has served in the House since December 1, 2022.

paragraphs.text: Rick Hillenbrand, whose given name is Frederick, was born in Staten Island, New York, and has lived in Hampshire County since 2011.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he graduated with honors from SUNY Maritime College and earned a Master of Science and an Ocean Engineer degree from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
He served in the U.S. Navy for more than 20 years, mostly as an Engineering Duty Officer, and retired as a commander from the Pentagon, where he was the Navy's program manager for its inactive fleet.
After the Navy he worked for several firms, including the NewPage pulp and paper mill in Luke, Maryland, from which he retired in 2013.

In the 2026 survey, Hillenbrand said he has helped secure permanent annual funding for volunteer fire departments and emergency medical services and led veterans' legislation as chair of the Veterans Caucus.

He listed his district priorities as reliable and affordable energy, data-center and transmission-line policy, clean drinking water, sewer and septic laws, entry- and mid-level housing, and economic development.
